title: Servicing Standard — How Remittances Are Applied on Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
**Status gate.** On a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage, a payment may be applied only while the loan is in active or nonaccrual status. The status is read from the loan's own system record, for the loan the remittance is made on; a loan in paid-off, applied or declined status takes no payment.

## Order of application

1. **Installment payments.** An installment payment pays the oldest unpaid installment first: its billed interest, and then its principal share (a scheduled principal payment), both entries pointing to the installment bill.
2. **Fees.** Fees are paid only when the remittance designates them, or after every billed installment is paid.
3. **Designated prepayments.** A remittance designated as a prepayment goes to principal as a prepayment only when no installment is past due.
4. **Payoffs.** A payoff pays fees, billed interest, interest from the day after the last due date through the payoff date (booked as a final accrual with the payoff date as its period end and its due date), any prepayment fee and all principal, the principal entry being marked as a payoff.

## Terms used

- **What an installment has been paid.** For one installment bill, the interest payments and the scheduled principal payments that point to that bill, less any returns of those payments.
- **Past-due installment.** An installment bill whose due date is earlier than the date considered and whose payments, so counted, are below the installment due.

## Points of judgement

| Situation | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Loan in active status | payment applied |
| Loan in nonaccrual status | payment applied |
| Loan in any other status | no payment applied |
| Remittance designated as a prepayment, no installment past due | principal prepayment |
| Remittance designated as a prepayment, an installment past due | not applied as a prepayment |
| Remittance not designating fees while a billed installment is unpaid | fees not paid from it |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** Two installments of USD 6000.00 each are unpaid on a loan in active status, each made of USD 2500.00 billed interest and USD 3500.00 principal share. A remittance of USD 9000.00 pays the older installment in full — USD 2500.00 interest, then USD 3500.00 principal, both pointing to that bill — and then the next: USD 2500.00 interest and USD 500.00 of its principal share. The newer installment remains past due if its due date has passed, so nothing is applied to fees unless they were designated.
